subtitle: Six carriers slip out of the Kurils
photoCredit: Zuikaku at Hitokappu Bay, November 1941, before the sortie. Japanese photo, public domain (Wikimedia Commons).
body:
Six aircraft carriers weigh anchor in a remote bay at the top of Japan this morning. Not one of them will send a radio signal until the job is done.

Akagi, Kaga, Soryu, Hiryu, Shokaku and Zuikaku leave Hitokappu Bay in the Kuril Islands under Vice Admiral Chuichi Nagumo, with battleships, cruisers and destroyers around them. Their course is east, into the empty North Pacific.

Half a world away in Washington, Secretary of State Cordell Hull hands Japan's envoys the American terms. Among them: Japan must pull its forces out of China and Indochina.
threads:
Six aircraft carriers weigh anchor in a remote bay at the top of Japan this morning, under strict radio silence.

Akagi, Kaga, Soryu, Hiryu, Shokaku and Zuikaku leave Hitokappu Bay in the Kurils and turn east into the empty North Pacific.

In Washington the same day, Cordell Hull hands Japan's envoys the American terms: get out of China and Indochina.

Pearl Harbor · Day 1 of 12
